**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 103, Verses 1–3**

**Explanation of the Words:**

"﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾" (By time): i.e., the whole of time (al-dahr).

"﴿إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ﴾" (Indeed, mankind): i.e., the whole human species.

"﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾" (is in loss): i.e., in deficiency and ruin, since his life is his capital. So if he dies without having believed and without having done righteous deeds, he has suffered the utmost loss.

"﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ﴾" (and enjoin one another to truth): i.e., they advise one another to hold to the truth in belief, in speech, and in action.

"﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾" (and enjoin one another to patience): i.e., they advise one another to be patient in holding to the truth in belief, in speech, and in action.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

Allah's words, ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ (By time). These three verses contain a judgment, one who is judged, and that by which he is judged. The judgment is what Allah has decreed upon man, all of mankind, of deficiency and loss. The one judged is man, the child of Adam. That by which he is judged is loss for the one who does not believe and does not do righteous deeds, and gain and salvation from loss for those who believe, do righteous deeds, enjoin one another to truth, and enjoin one another to patience.

So Allah's words ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ are an oath that Allah swears by time, meaning the whole of time, its night and its day, its morning and its evening. The answer to the oath is Allah's words ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ (Indeed, mankind is in loss), i.e., in deficiency, destruction, and ruin, for he lives in toil (kabad) and dies and goes to Hell, losing everything, even the self between his two sides.

And His words ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ (except those who believe and do righteous deeds). Allah excepts these from loss, so they are gainers, not losers, by their entry into Paradise, the abode of happiness. By faith is meant belief in Allah and His Messenger and in what the Messenger brought of guidance and the religion of truth. By righteous deeds are meant the obligatory acts (fara'id), the recommended practices (sunan), and the voluntary acts (nawafil).

His words ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ mean: in its belief, speech, and action, which is by following the Book and the Sunnah. His words ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ mean: they advise one another to hold to the truth in belief, speech, and action, and to be patient in that until one of them dies while believing in the truth, speaking by it, and acting upon what came in it. Islam is true, the Book is true, and the Messenger is true. By this they believe, act, and enjoin one another to remain steadfast in that until death.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The virtue of Surah al-'Asr, for it contains the path of salvation in three verses. So much so that Imam al-Shafi'i said: "If Allah had sent down no proof to His creation except this surah, it would have sufficed them."

2. An explanation of the fate of the disbeliever, which is total loss.

3. An explanation of the triumph of the people of faith and righteous deeds, who avoid shirk and sins.

4. The obligation of enjoining one another to truth and enjoining one another to patience among the Muslims.
